If there is no replacement, return 404/410 with a helpful page.

suggested_action.verification: curl -s https://<host>/ | grep -c '"Organization"' >= 1.
steps: Add Organization with name, url, description, address, contactPoint; legalName, logo and foundingDate are optional.
Add WebSite with url, name and a potentialAction SearchAction pointing at your site-search URL template.
Use one @id (e.g. https://example.com/#organization) and reference it from every page that names the organisation, so the whole site resolves to one entity.

generator.mode: read-only audit; recommendations only; no site modification

overall.interpretation: Little of the site's content was readable, reachable or stated in a form a machine can quote; the findings say which.

prioritized_actions.title: Stop collapsing unknown or retired URLs onto the home page.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Deep links are redirected to the home page
prioritized_actions.mechanism: A home-page catch-all breaks the continuity between the answer and the visit, and it means arbitrary URLs under the host return 200 rather than 404, so retired addresses stay indistinguishable from live ones.
steps: Redirect a retired product to its closest live replacement, not to the home page.
If there is no replacement, return 404/410 with a helpful page.
Never use a catch-all rewrite for unmatched routes.
prioritized_actions.verification: Each URL listed resolves to its own content or returns 404.

prioritized_actions.title: Pick one canonical brand string and use it byte-identically everywhere.
prioritized_actions.addresses: The brand is called different things in different places on its own site
prioritized_actions.mechanism: One exact string in Organization.name, og:site_name, the title suffix and Product.brand is an explicit statement that every mention is the same entity; several strings leave that to be inferred.
steps: Choose the exact trading name, including capitalisation and any suffix.
Use it in Organization.name, og:site_name, the <title> suffix, the footer copyright and Product.brand.name.
Put the legal entity name in legalName, not in name.
Roll the same string out to every off-site profile.
prioritized_actions.verification: Grep the rendered home page for the brand string; every occurrence should be identical.

prioritized_actions.title: Serve one price per product from a single source, on every surface.
prioritized_actions.addresses: The same product is priced differently on the listing and on its own page
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Two prices for one product is an internal contradiction: nothing in the markup says which is current, so a reader of either page has no basis to pick. One source removes the disagreement.
steps: Render listing tiles and product pages from the same pricing service call, not from a denormalised copy.
Invalidate listing caches when a product price changes.
Add a nightly consistency job that diffs listing vs detail prices.
prioritized_actions.verification: A crawl of every category page reports zero price mismatches against the linked product pages.

prioritized_actions.title: Make each page canonical to itself unless it is a genuine duplicate.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Canonical tags collapse content pages onto the home page
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Product detail pages whose canonical is the home page state that their content is the home page's; a self-referencing canonical states, explicitly, that each page is its own preferred address.
steps: Remove hardcoded canonicals from shared templates.
Generate the canonical from the page's own route, not from a site-wide constant.
prioritized_actions.verification: For each URL listed, the canonical equals the URL itself.

prioritized_actions.title: Render at least the aggregate rating and a few reviews server-side.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Reviews appear to be loaded by a client-side widget, so the proof is invisible to a fetch
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Third-party review widgets inject their content after load, so the rating exists in the rendered page and not in the server response; rendering it server-side puts the same value in the bytes a fetch receives.
steps: Ask the review vendor for their SEO/server-rendered snippet or API.
Fetch the aggregate at build/render time and emit it in the HTML plus AggregateRating markup.
Render the newest 3-5 review bodies server-side; keep pagination client-side.
Never mark up a rating the page does not actually display.
prioritized_actions.verification: curl -s <product url> | grep -i 'ratingValue' returns a value.

prioritized_actions.title: Move the attributes already published into a specification structure.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Product attributes are not presented in a standardized specification structure
prioritized_actions.mechanism: A two-column structure with one row per attribute makes the same attribute addressable at the same place on every product page, so values can be compared across the range without interpreting a sentence differently on each page.
steps: Use a real <table> or <dl> with one row per attribute, including units - starting with the attributes these pages already publish: '<Attribute>'.
Keep the same attribute set, in the same order, across the category so rows line up between products.
State the negative values too, not only the positive ones - an explicitly absent property cannot be inferred as present.
Mirror the same values in additionalProperty markup so the visible table and the typed data agree.
prioritized_actions.verification: curl -s <product-url> shows a <table> or <dl> whose rows are the attribute names.

prioritized_actions.title: Fix or remove the broken sitemap references.
prioritized_actions.addresses: A declared sitemap is missing or does not parse
prioritized_actions.mechanism: A declared sitemap is the site's own statement of which URLs exist; one that does not parse, or is not there, states nothing, so the URLs it was meant to list are discoverable only by following links.
steps: Remove Sitemap: lines pointing at URLs that 404.
Validate the XML (a stray & or an unescaped < will break the whole file).
If a sitemap index lists children, make sure every child resolves.
If the sitemap is served but refuses unknown user-agents, allow crawlers to read it - a sitemap only a browser can fetch helps no crawler.
prioritized_actions.verification: Every URL in every Sitemap: directive returns 200 and valid XML.

prioritized_actions.title: Publish a stable sku plus a global identifier (GTIN or MPN) on every product.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Products carry no stable identifier, so listings elsewhere cannot be matched to them
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Corroboration works by matching entities across sources. Without a shared identifier there is no field on which your page and a retailer's listing are the same product, so the two never reinforce each other and neither becomes the trusted answer.
steps: Emit sku (your internal code) on every Product.
Emit gtin13/gtin12/gtin8 where a barcode exists, mpn otherwise.
Use the same identifier in your merchant feeds and marketplace listings so they resolve to one entity.
Keep the identifier stable across price changes and re-designs.
prioritized_actions.verification: Search a GTIN from your catalogue; your own page and your retail partners' listings should both surface.

prioritized_actions.title: Publish the product's attributes as a specification block and mirror them in additionalProperty.
prioritized_actions.addresses: A buyer asking about a product's specifications finds no answer in the fetched evidence
prioritized_actions.mechanism: A question is answerable when the fact is present in the response and identifiable without guessing. Publishing it once, in a typed field, makes every phrasing of the question resolvable from the same value.
steps: Publish the product's attributes as a specification block and mirror them in additionalProperty.
prioritized_actions.verification: Re-run this audit; the question moves out of not_answerable in the answerability matrix.

prioritized_actions.title: Give each product page enough plain-text substance to answer a question.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Product pages carry very little extractable text
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Plain-text substance is what a question can be matched against; a page with a title, a price and three bullet points states almost nothing to match.
steps: Add a 100-200 word description that states what the product is, who it is for and what makes it different - in plain sentences.
Publish the full specification as text (not an image or a PDF).
Include the questions buyers actually ask, with answers.
Keep the text in the server response, not in a tab loaded on click.
prioritized_actions.verification: curl -s <url> | wc -w exceeds ~400 for a product page.

prioritized_actions.title: Emit a truthful <lastmod> for every sitemap URL.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Sitemap entries omit <lastmod>, so the sitemap says nothing about what changed
prioritized_actions.mechanism: lastmod is the sitemap's own statement of what changed and when. Without it the sitemap gives a reader no basis to tell a page that changed this morning from one untouched for two years.
steps: Set lastmod from the content's real modification timestamp.
Use W3C datetime format with a timezone.
Update it whenever a stated fact on the page changes, not only on copy edits.
prioritized_actions.verification: Change one page, regenerate the sitemap, and confirm only that URL's lastmod moved.

prioritized_actions.title: Repair or remove the missing URLs from sitemaps and internal links.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Pages the site itself advertises are not there
prioritized_actions.mechanism: A URL the site advertises and then answers with 404 or 410 is a statement the site contradicts itself on; each one is a request spent on a page that did not serve.
steps: Either restore the page or 301 it to the closest live equivalent.
Regenerate the sitemap so it no longer lists missing URLs.
Add a build-time check that every sitemap URL returns 200.
prioritized_actions.verification: Re-crawl: zero 404/410 among sitemap-listed and internally linked URLs.

prioritized_actions.title: Fill out the Organization entity with the properties that apply to it.
prioritized_actions.addresses: The Organization entity is declared but omits properties a site of this shape is expected to carry
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Entity resolution works by matching attributes. A node with only a name matches every company sharing that name; a node with a description, contact details and, where it has one, an address provides explicit machine-readable evidence to match on.
steps: Add description (one factual sentence, no marketing).
Add a PostalAddress for the organisation's location.
Add a ContactPoint (or telephone/email).
Add sameAs for every official profile the site links to.
Add legalName when it differs from the trading name.
Give the node a stable @id such as https://example.com/#organization and reference it from every page that names the organisation.
prioritized_actions.verification: Structured-data test shows an Organization carrying the properties listed as expected.

prioritized_actions.title: Set "@context": "https://schema.org" on every JSON-LD block.
prioritized_actions.addresses: JSON-LD blocks do not declare the schema.org context
prioritized_actions.mechanism: Without the context, `"@type": "Product"` is an undefined term rather than schema.org's Product, so the block carries no meaning to a consumer.
steps: Use the https:// form of the context URL.
If you use @graph, put @context once at the top level.
prioritized_actions.verification: Every ld+json block contains schema.org in its @context.

prioritized_actions.title: Publish the attributes this catalogue already states as typed properties.
prioritized_actions.addresses: Product pages expose no typed schema.org attributes
prioritized_actions.mechanism: A PropertyValue with a name, a value and a unit is comparable across products without interpretation. The same fact in prose has to be located and parsed first, and that step is where it is dropped.
steps: Add an additionalProperty PropertyValue entry for each attribute these pages already publish: '<Attribute>'.
Use the first-class properties where schema.org has one: color, size, material, weight, width, height.
Keep the typed value and the visible value identical - the markup must describe what the page displays.
State the negative facts as well as the positive ones; an attribute that is absent from the markup is not readable as 'no', only as 'unknown'.
prioritized_actions.verification: The Product JSON-LD on a product page contains an additionalProperty entry for each attribute the page displays, with matching values.

proactive_recommendations.title: Publish comparison and 'which one for what' pages for the range you sell
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: A page whose heading is the question and whose body is a comparison table states the answer to a constrained question explicitly, in one place, where a listing states only the range. That provides a page that can be quoted and linked to for that question; whether any system retrieves it is not something this audit measures.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: The site sells a range (two or more sellable items of the same kind (physical: 3)) and comparison-shaped content is the direct way to state how its items differ.
steps: List the 10-20 questions your buyers actually ask, from support tickets, on-site search logs and marketplace Q&A. This audit generates its questions from your content, not from anyone's behaviour, so your own sources are the ones that know.
Publish comparison and 'best <item> for <use>' pages, each at its own URL with the question as the heading and a direct answer in the first paragraph (e.g. about Northvale Press).
Include an HTML <table> comparing the items on the attributes the question cares about, with units, and link each row to its own page.
Mark the page up with FAQPage or ItemList as appropriate and keep it updated.
proactive_recommendations.verification: Re-ask the same questions in a browsing-enabled assistant, monthly, and record whether the page is cited.

applicability.applies_because: two or more sellable items of the same kind (physical: 3), on a ecommerce site
conditions: two or more comparable sellable items were read
applicability.evidence_requirement: two or more comparable sellable items were read

proactive_recommendations.title: Make every deep link land on the specific page it names
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: A visitor who arrives by a link was pointed at something specific. A deep link that resolves to the exact page, with the decisive fact stated early in the server-rendered HTML, provides that fact at the point of arrival instead of leaving it to be searched for. How often visitors arrive this way, and what they do next, is not something this audit measures.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: Every quotable fact on the site is a potential landing page, and a landing page that answers the question it was linked for needs nothing else.
steps: Deep-link from every quotable fact to the exact product page, never the home page, and never collapse retired URLs onto the front door.
Keep what the page exists to state - the price and whether it is available - in the first screen of server-rendered markup, before long-form copy.
Where a documented intent parameter is read (for example ?intent=...), server-render the matching one-line context strip; use first-party storage only.
Give each section a breadcrumb and onward links so a near-miss landing has a path to the right page.
proactive_recommendations.verification: Segment analytics by referrer and compare bounce rate and time-to-first-interaction against organic search.

applicability.applies_because: 5 deep content pages were read on a ecommerce site
conditions: two or more deep content pages read
applicability.evidence_requirement: two or more deep content pages were read

proactive_recommendations.title: Stand up a recurring answer-monitoring set instead of auditing once
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: A fixed question set turned into a weekly measurement converts 'are we visible?' from an opinion into a series of observations that can be compared over time; this audit makes one such observation, of the site alone.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: This audit is a point-in-time snapshot; the gaps it detects recur silently.
steps: Freeze ~30 questions in your own nouns: 10 category questions, 10 brand-fact questions (return window, delivery time, who you are), and 10 product questions, for example 'is Northvale Press available, and what does it cost?'.
Run them weekly across at least three assistants with browsing enabled.
Record three numbers per question: organisation mentioned (y/n), correct fact (y/n), own domain cited (y/n).
Re-run this audit on the same cadence and track the pillar scores and the finding count alongside.
proactive_recommendations.verification: A dated spreadsheet or dashboard showing mention-rate, fact-accuracy and citation-rate for 127.0.0.1:34559 over time.

conditions: none: a standing practice for any site that wants to know how its published facts are being read
applicability.evidence_requirement: none - a standing practice for any site

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose a public, versioned product data feed at a stable URL
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: Page-by-page crawling samples a catalogue; a feed states it. A single crawlable feed provides every item's price, availability and identifier in one machine-readable document, so a change is visible in one fetch instead of a re-crawl of every page. Which consumers read feeds is not measured here.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: Product pages exist, so the catalogue data already exists in a database - publishing it costs one endpoint.
steps: Publish /feeds/products.json (and optionally a merchant-centre style feed) with sku, gtin, mpn, name, brand, category, price, currency, availability, canonical URL, image, and lastModified per item.
Serve it uncompressed under 10MB per file, paginate with a next link if larger.
Reference the feed from robots.txt as a comment and from /llms.txt.
Regenerate on every price or stock change, never on a nightly-only cadence.
proactive_recommendations.verification: Diff the feed against three live product pages; price, availability and title must match exactly.

applicability.applies_because: 3 product page(s) selling physical or digital goods with a price were read
conditions: two or more product pages selling goods with a price
applicability.evidence_requirement: physical or digital goods sold with priced offers

proactive_recommendations.title: Publish an agent-facing index (/llms.txt or /agents.md) of the pages you want quoted
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: An agent-facing index is a plain-text, machine-readable map naming which URLs carry the canonical answer to the questions the site is asked. It provides explicit evidence of where the facts are, on one fetch; how any given agent uses it, or whether it reads it at all, is not something this audit measures.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: Neither convention was served during this audit (probed: http://127.0.0.1:34559/llms.txt, http://127.0.0.1:34559/agents.md).
steps: Create /llms.txt with an H1 of the organisation's name and a one-line description.
List, as markdown links with a short gloss each: the brand fact page, the top product pages, the category hubs, shipping, returns, warranty and FAQ.
Keep every linked page server-rendered and under the same canonical host.
Link it from robots.txt with a comment and list it in your sitemap so it is discoverable without guessing the path.
If you prefer the /agents.md convention, publish that instead - one is enough, and both should say the same thing if you ship both.
proactive_recommendations.verification: curl -s https://127.0.0.1:34559/llms.txt | head -40 returns the index, and each linked URL returns 200 with the fact visible in the raw HTML.

proactive_recommendations.title: Link the organisation to an independent knowledge-base entry where one exists or is warranted
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: A knowledge-base or registry entry is an independent, machine-readable description of the organisation, and a sameAs pointing at it is the explicit statement that the two are the same entity. That provides evidence a similarly named organisation cannot be confused with; whether any system uses it is not something this audit measures.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: No outbound link to a knowledge-base entry about the organisation, and no sameAs, was found in the crawled pages.
steps: Check whether a registry or knowledge-base entry already exists (a company register, a research or organisation identifier, an encyclopaedia article), and declare it in Organization.sameAs.
Where none exists and the organisation meets the relevant notability and conflict-of-interest rules, follow each knowledge base's own process - never author an entry covertly.
Use one exact official name string on the site and in every entry.
proactive_recommendations.verification: Organization.sameAs lists at least one knowledge-base or registry entry that names this organisation.

proactive_recommendations.title: Run a correction pass over the third-party copies of your facts
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: Facts about an organisation are repeated on sites it does not control, and a correction made only on its own site leaves every older copy stating the old fact. Correcting the copies provides the same fact in every place it is stated; how any system weighs agreement between sources is not something this audit measures.
proactive_recommendations.why_now: Updating the site is necessary but not sufficient: copies of its facts live off-site, and this audit can only see what the site itself declares.
steps: Inventory where your facts are repeated: retailer listings, marketplaces, comparison sites, review aggregators and directories.

For each, submit the correction through that source's own supported channel - a listing or profile claim, a partner or seller portal where one exists, an editorial correction request - never by scraping or editing anything you do not own.
Publish a dated changelog page for renames, rebrands and discontinuations so third parties have something citable to point at.
Re-check the highest-traffic ten sources quarterly.
proactive_recommendations.verification: Count of third-party sources stating the current fact, tracked quarterly.
